name: HTF Top-Down Pullback Strategy
description: Trader's D1->H4->H1->M15->M5 top-down flow. SMA(6,20,100) as key S&R/POI/targets. Pullback entries off HTF exhaustion + LTF structure shift, with ghost-wick/chase/ATR-distance filters. Signal types: Sniper zone-to-zone, Structure Shift + Rejection, Zone Reaction, Pullback, Trend Entry, Re-Entry, Tier 3 Confluence.
content:
ACTIVATION: this is a strategy skill, not a default -- only follow it while it is genuinely marked as the active trading strategy. When active, follow it EXPLICITLY: use only the timeframes and endpoints named below. Do not supplement with other timeframes, indicators, or endpoints "just to be safe" -- that is trading a different strategy, not extra diligence.

## Top-down flow
Read in this order, every time, before any entry: D1 -> H4 -> H1 -> M15 -> M5. The higher timeframe (D1/H4/H1) sets the real directional bias. M15 and M5 are for finding and timing the entry only. Never take an entry that fights the HTF bias -- if D1/H4/H1 disagree with each other, stand down rather than forcing a read.

Map directly to real tools: pull get_trend and get_structure on D1, H4, and H1 to establish bias. Pull get_structure, get_swing, and get_candles on M15 and M5 for the entry mechanics below.

## Market structure
Track HH/HL (bullish structure) and LH/LL (bearish structure) using real WICK highs and lows, not candle bodies -- get_swing and get_candles both report real wick highs/lows, use those, not close-to-close ranges. A structure shift is a CHoCH on M5, M15, or M30 -- get_structure's real choch field is the source of truth for this, not a visual guess.

## SMA levels (6, 20, 100) as S&R
These are the real key support/resistance zones, and Dave's get_trend endpoint already computes them natively as smma6/smma20/smma100 (SMMA, the trader's own trend system) -- use those real fields directly, do not recompute. Price tapping the 6 SMMA often produces a real bounce; a tap of the 20 or 100 SMMA is a stronger reaction. All three double as POI (point of interest) for entries and as real target levels for exits.

## Pullback setup, the core entry mechanism
1. HTF (D1/H4/H1) is in a real trend, per get_trend's bias.
2. Price shows real exhaustion -- a genuine rejection wick, visible in get_candles' wick-to-body ratio for the current/recent candle on the HTF being read.
3. On the LTF (M15 then M5), price starts printing real lower highs/lows (for a sell pullback) or higher highs/lows (for a buy pullback) -- confirmed via get_structure/get_swing on that timeframe, not assumed.
4. Target is the HTF's own 6 SMMA or 20 SMMA level (from get_trend on the HTF being traded off).
5. Entry triggers when the LTF (M5) genuinely breaks structure toward that SMA target, confirmed by a real rejection or institutional candle (get_patterns' institutional_candle field, or a real wick rejection at the level) -- never an entry on a break alone without that confirmation.

## Entry filters -- all four must clear, every time
- H1 ghost wick: reject a buy if the H1 candle's upper wick is more than 60% of its total real range (a real rejection candle worth respecting, not a level to fade into) -- read this from get_candles on H1.
- No chasing wicks on M5: wait for the real M5 candle CLOSE before acting on a break or rejection -- never enter mid-wick before the candle actually closes.
- ATR distance filter: check get_volatility's ATR on the entry timeframe -- if price has already run further than a reasonable ATR multiple from the last real structure point, do not chase it; that move is spent, wait for the next setup.
- SMA retest: wait for price to genuinely pull back and tap the M15 6 or 20 SMMA with a real rejection (wick into it, close back out) before entering -- a break of structure with no retest of the SMA target zone is not yet a complete setup.

## Signal types this strategy covers
All of these share the same top-down flow, SMA-zone logic, and entry filters above -- they are labels for the setup shape, not seven separate rule sets:
- Sniper: a real zone-to-zone move, roughly 100/200/300 pips depending on the instrument's real volatility (check get_volatility for a sane real distance on this specific symbol, never a blind pip count).
- Structure Shift + Rejection: a real CHoCH followed immediately by a rejection at the new level.
- Zone Reaction: price reacting off a real SMA/POI zone without a full pullback sequence.
- Pullback: the full core mechanism described above.
- Trend Entry: a continuation entry in the HTF's own direction, same filters apply.
- Re-Entry: a second entry in the same direction after a prior one closed, only valid if the HTF bias and structure still genuinely support it -- never a reflexive re-entry just because the first one worked.
- Tier 3 Confluence: multiple of the above signal types agreeing on the same zone/timeframe at once -- the highest-conviction version of this strategy, size accordingly per trading.md's own conviction scale.

SL/TP and position sizing still follow trading.md exactly as written -- this skill governs WHICH setups to look for and HOW to read the chart, not risk management, which stays built-in and unchanged.
